rationale: The phrase 'not less than any candidate value' has two relevant transcriptions: conventional >=, or literal negation of <. They differ for NaN, which the response itself names without resolving its oracle treatment. Both retain the explicitly stated no-earlier-equal condition. The fallback mentions unsupported exceptional states but does not define which states are unsupported; do not invent an all-finite admission guard. Check both literal predicate readings while leaving classical verification/fallback and whole-task behavior unjudged.

interpretations.meaning: Conventional non-strict ordering interpretation of not-less, with first equal index.
interpretations.expression: all(values[i] >= values[k] for k in indices) and not any(values[j] == values[i] for j in indices if j < i)

interpretations.meaning: Negate strict less-than literally; retain no earlier equal value.
interpretations.expression: not any(values[i] < values[k] for k in indices) and not any(values[j] == values[i] for j in indices if j < i)
